title: Solid spectral analytic coefficients
summary: Light solid spectral foundations, countable product/tower and balanced tensor comparisons, cardinal interchange, complete filtered null families, bounded-below realizations and spectral analytic coefficients, preserving the sphere and the relocated RefinedTraceMethods foundation.

layers.title: Light spectral sheaves and the null-sequence test

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.lightSpectralSheaves
targets.statement: Fix a small skeleton of second-countable profinite spaces in universe u, with finite jointly surjective covering families. Define Cond(Sp) as hypercomplete spectrum-valued sheaves on this site. Construct a presentable stable closed symmetric monoidal enhancement, with tensor obtained by hypersheafifying the sectionwise tensor. Its limits are sectionwise; its colimits are hypersheafified sectionwise colimits. Construct the free spectral sheaf 𝕊[T] representing evaluation at each light profinite T. Prove that hypercovers can be refined by simplicial light profinite objects, so each descent comparison involves a countable diagram.
hypotheses: u is fixed and diagrams are u-small; spectra live in a compatible enlargement
the coherent site uses finite covers; hyperdescent is required

locator.where: Definition 4.0.1, pp.27–28, RC line 1392; W paragraph 2.1, p.11, W line 437

api.name: lightSpectralFree
api.statement: For each light profinite T, the free object has Map(𝕊[T],M) ≃ M(T), naturally in T and M.

api.name: lightSpectralSheaves_ext
api.statement: Maps agree when their maps of values agree coherently on the site; equivalences are detected on all values.

api.name: lightSpectralSheaves_descent
api.statement: For every hypercover U•→T, M(T)→Tot M(U•) is an equivalence.

api.name: lightSpectralTensor
api.statement: The free-object tensor is 𝕊[T]⊗𝕊[U] ≃ 𝕊[T×U], including empty T or U.

tests.name: empty
tests.statement: The empty space evaluates to 0, excluding the constant presheaf with nonzero empty value.

tests.name: pair
tests.statement: For a disjoint pair, the sheaf value is two factors, and the free object is two spheres.

tests.name: ordinary_carrier
tests.statement: The degree-zero integer homotopy sheaves use LightCondAb; an ordinary Category-valued sheaf alone does not encode spectral hyperdescent.

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.discreteSpectralAdjunction
targets.statement: For every spectrum X construct δX as the hypercomplete constant sheaf. Prove δ ⊣ ev_* with unit X→(δX)(*) an equivalence, and δ𝕊≃𝕊 and δ(X⊗Y)≃δX⊗δY coherently. Hence δ is fully faithful and preserves all small colimits. Identify the homotopy sheaf π_k(δX) with the discrete sheaf on π_kX for every integer k. The comparison from δ of an inverse limit to the limit of δ is a specified natural map, with no general equivalence assertion.
hypotheses: X,Y are arbitrary spectra, without boundedness restrictions

locator.where: Paragraph 2.1, p.11, W line 437; MW paragraph 4.1, p.41, MW line 1748

api.name: discreteSpectral_map
api.statement: A spectral map X→Y induces δX→δY, preserving identities, composites, zero maps and all integer shifts.

api.name: discreteSpectral_unit
api.statement: The adjunction unit is the natural equivalence X→(δX)(*), including its action on every π_k.

api.name: discreteSpectral_tensor
api.statement: The tensor and unit comparisons of δ satisfy symmetry, associativity and unit coherences.

tests.name: zero
tests.statement: δ0=0 and the adjunction unit at 0 is the identity of 0.

tests.name: two_terms
tests.statement: For X=𝕊⊕Σ𝕊, π₀δX is ℤ and π₁δX contains the shifted ℤ summand.

tests.name: inverse_limit
tests.statement: The inverse limit of discrete H(ℤ/p^r) has continuous ℤ_p-valued sections. On T=ℤ_p its identity section is not locally constant, so it is not δHℤ_p.

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.spectralNullSequence
targets.statement: Let C=ℕ∪{∞} with the one-point compactification topology, and define N=cofib(𝕊[{∞}]→𝕊[C]). Define σ:N→N from the continuous map n↦n+1, ∞↦∞, using its compatibility with the marked point. All maps and cofibers are in Cond(Sp). Construct the universe-lifted marked compactification and compare the free integer null summand, shift and internal projectivity with the pinned Type0 model. At the base universe, internal projectivity is imported; the additional target is its natural scalar/site transport on the common light presentations, not another base-universe proof.
hypotheses: the point ∞ is marked; ℕ is indexed from 0

locator.where: Paragraph 2.1, p.11, W line 443; RC Definition 3.2.1, p.16, RC line 730

api.name: spectralNullSequence_map
api.statement: A continuous map of pointed compactifications induces the corresponding map of cofibers, with identity and composition laws.

api.name: spectralNullSequence_hom
api.statement: Internal Hom from N to M is the fiber of internal Hom(𝕊[C],M)→internal Hom(𝕊[{∞}],M).

api.name: spectralNullSequence_shift
api.statement: For a map with coefficient sequence b, precomposition σ* has coefficient at n equal to b_(n+1).

api.name: spectralNullSequence_universe
api.statement: On common light presentations, universe/scalar lifts commute with the marked point, null summand and shift and transport the integer internal-projectivity lifting test.

tests.name: marked_point
tests.statement: The free cofiber on a singleton marked point is 0, excluding an unreduced free object.

tests.name: shift
tests.statement: Against δHℤ, (1−σ*)e₁=e₁−e₀ and its inverse sends e₁ to e₁+e₀.

tests.name: direction
tests.statement: A right shift on coefficient sequences sends e₁ to e₂ and fails the computed witness.

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.isSolidSpectrum
targets.statement: A spectrum-valued hypersheaf M is solid when 1−σ* is an equivalence of internal Hom objects Hom(N,M)→Hom(N,M). Define Sp■ as the full subcategory on this property. Equivalently, M is right-orthogonal to cofib(1−σ:N→N) after tensoring that cofiber with every free 𝕊[T]; the internal and externally tested formulations must agree.
hypotheses: M is a light spectral hypersheaf; all T range over the chosen light site

locator.where: Paragraph 2.1, p.11, W lines 443–451; MW paragraph 4.1, MW line 1754

api.name: isSolidSpectrum_iff_tests
api.statement: Solidity is equivalent to Map(cofib(1−σ)⊗𝕊[T],M)=0 for every T.

api.name: isSolidSpectrum_equiv
api.statement: An equivalence of hypersheaves transports solidity; the full-subcategory inclusion is fully faithful.

api.name: discrete_isSolidSpectrum
api.statement: Every δX is solid for arbitrary X, with the finite-support inverse of 1−σ* agreeing with the integer witness.

tests.name: zero
tests.statement: 0 is solid, with the unique self-map of its zero Hom an equivalence.

tests.name: sphere
tests.statement: δ𝕊 is solid with π₀=ℤ and π₁=ℤ/2; replacing spectra by Hℤ-modules loses the latter sphere class.

tests.name: free_null
tests.statement: N is not solid: its pointwise π₀ is ⊕_ℕℤ, whereas its solidification has product π₀ and contains the all-one vector.

layers.title: Solidification, homotopy and the compact generator

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.solidHomotopyTStructure
targets.statement: First prove, inside Cond(Sp), that Hom(N,−) is t-exact and preserves small colimits; its homotopy sheaf in degree k is the internal abelian Hom from the integer null object to π_k. Deduce that M is solid exactly when every π_kM is integer-solid on the light site. The homotopy t-structure restricts to the stable full subcategory Sp■, has heart the light realization of SolidAb, is nondegenerate and left and right complete, and is compatible with filtered colimits and countable products. Compare truncations and shifts with ordinary spectra and the supplied integer enhancement.
hypotheses: all homotopy indices and lower bounds are integers
the light site is fixed; countable products and Postnikov limits use this site

locator.where: Theorem 2.3.3(1)–(3), pp.12–13, RC line 537; Theorem 3.2.4(6), p.17, RC line 764; proof RC line 870 (integer model)

api.name: solidHomotopy_truncation
api.statement: All homotopy truncations preserve solidity; their unit/counit maps have the stated π_k isomorphism and vanishing ranges.

api.name: solidHomotopy_heart
api.statement: The heart inclusion identifies a solid integer group B with HB, with π₀=B and all other homotopy sheaves zero.

api.name: solidHomotopy_shift
api.statement: Suspension sends the lower bound b to b+1 and gives π_k(ΣM)=π_(k−1)M.

tests.name: shift
tests.statement: ΣHℤ has π₁=ℤ and π₀=0; cohomological ℤ in degree 2 corresponds to π₋₂=ℤ.

tests.name: zero
tests.statement: The zero module lies in every connective and coconnective range.

tests.name: square_zero
tests.statement: A=𝕊⊕Σ𝕊 with square-zero ideal is connective and has a nonzero π₁; its heart does not determine A as a spectral algebra.

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.solidSpectralReflection
targets.statement: Construct the accessible reflection L■:Cond(Sp)→Sp■. Prove that the inclusion creates all small limits and colimits and that Hom(C,M) is solid whenever M is solid and C is any condensed spectrum. Prove tensor compatibility L■(C⊗D)≃L■(L■C⊗D), and equip Sp■ with closed symmetric monoidal tensor C⊗■D=L■(C⊗D), unit δ𝕊 and the ambient internal Hom into solid targets. Prove L■ preserves connective objects. For a connective E₁ solid A, Mod_A has the underlying homotopy t-structure. For connective commutative A, tensor over A sends degrees ≥b and ≥c to degrees ≥b+c, for all integers b,c. For every light profinite T presented as a sequential limit of finite quotients T_n, construct L■𝕊[T]≃lim_n δ𝕊[T_n], independent of the presentation and compatible with its free-object unit.
hypotheses: C,D range over Cond(Sp); M is solid

locator.where: Paragraph 2.1, p.11, W lines 448–451; RC Theorem 3.2.4(5)–(8), p.17, RC line 761 (integer model); RC Theorem 3.2.4(12), p.17, RC line 773 (free measure model)

api.name: solidSpectralReflection_unit
api.statement: For solid M, precomposition with C→L■C gives Map(L■C,M)≃Map(C,M); its counit is invertible.

api.name: solidSpectralReflection_idempotent
api.statement: The two units L■C→L■L■C agree and are equivalences.

api.name: solidSpectralTensorHom
api.statement: For solid C,D,M, Hom(C⊗■D,M)≃Hom(C,Hom(D,M)), coherently with symmetry and units.

api.name: solidSpectralFreeMeasure
api.statement: For every sequential finite-quotient presentation of T, the free solid measure object is the displayed limit; its unit is induced by the finite projections, and maps of T act covariantly.

tests.name: unit
tests.statement: L■δ𝕊=δ𝕊, and δ𝕊⊗■M=M.

tests.name: hom
tests.statement: Internal Hom into a solid target is computed in Cond(Sp), rather than by forgetting condensation.

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.integerLinearSolidComparison
targets.statement: Construct a symmetric monoidal t-exact equivalence Mod_{δHℤ}(Sp■)≃D(SolidAb_light) on the common enhancement. It identifies solidification of Hℤ-module sheaves with derived integer solidification, including the units and the internal-Hom comparison. For every integer b and solid X with π_kX=0 for all k<b, the unit-induced map X→δHℤ⊗■X induces an isomorphism on π_b. Consequently Hℤ⊗■− detects zero objects among bounded-below solid spectra. Compare modules over θB for animated B through the supplied animated-to-commutative-algebra functor, without identifying animated rings with arbitrary connective spectral algebras.
hypotheses: the same light site and size-bounded integer realization are used on both sides
the conservativity assertion requires a lower homotopy bound
B uses the supplied θ, with its rational-only equivalence restriction

locator.where: Paragraph 4.1, p.41, MW line 1763; RC Theorem 3.2.4(9)–(11), p.17, RC line 769

tests.name: integer
tests.statement: The spectral Hℤ-module unit corresponds to ℤ concentrated in cohomological degree 0.

tests.name: tor
tests.statement: H𝔽_p⊗_{Hℤ}H𝔽_p has π₀=π₁=𝔽_p and other homotopy zero, including p=2,3.

tests.name: animation
tests.statement: Over 𝔽₂, a free commutative derived algebra retains positive symmetric-group homology, whereas the animated polynomial algebra is discrete.

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.solidNullCompactGenerator
targets.statement: Put G=L■N. Construct an equivalence G≃∏_ℕδ𝕊, with the product in Cond(Sp), and prove G is connective, compact and a generator of Sp■. For any E₁ algebra A, G_A=A⊗■G is a compact generator of left A-modules. For connective A it is connective and its degree-zero homotopy is a projective generator of the heart. The homotopy sheaves of G are ∏_ℕδπ_k𝕊, and Hℤ⊗■G corresponds to ∏_ℕℤ. For connective A, Map_A(G_A,−) is t-exact and the endomorphism spectrum R_A=Map_A(G_A,G_A) is connective; precomposition makes Map_A(G_A,M) a right R_A-module.
hypotheses: A may be noncommutative; connectivity conclusions require connective A
compactness means preservation of all filtered colimits by the mapping spectrum

locator.where: Paragraph 2.3, p.12, W line 472; RC Theorem 3.2.4(12), p.17, RC line 773 (integer model)

api.name: solidNullGenerator_unit
api.statement: The map N→G is the reflection unit and its maps to the finite partition quotients determine the product comparison.

api.name: solidNullGenerator_homotopy
api.statement: For every integer k, π_kG=∏ℕδπ_k𝕊, with the finite-coordinate evaluation maps.

api.name: solidModuleGenerator_free
api.statement: For every E₁ A, Map_A(A⊗■G,M)=Map(G,UM); this transports compactness and zero detection.

tests.name: point
tests.statement: At the point, π₀G=∏_ℕℤ and the all-one vector is present.

tests.name: non_discrete
tests.statement: The null family e_n gives a continuous map of the convergent sequence to π₀G; as a map into the discrete group ∏_ℕℤ it is not continuous.

tests.name: zero_algebra
tests.statement: For A=0 the module category and G_A are both zero; generation is still the zero-object detection assertion.

layers.title: Countable products, split towers and balanced tensor

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.countableProductTensor
targets.statement: For all countable sets I,J, including finite and empty sets, the projection-induced map (∏_Iδ𝕊)⊗■(∏_Jδ𝕊)→∏_(I×J)δ𝕊 is an equivalence, natural under reindexing and coherent with units, symmetry and associativity. Identify the map on integer-linearization with VS2.1’s derived product tensor.
hypotheses: I and J are countable in the fixed universe

locator.where: Proof of Lemma B.8, printed p.79, Q line 3672; RC Theorem 3.2.4(13), p.17, RC line 777

tests.name: empty
tests.statement: If I=∅ the empty product in the stable category is 0, so both sides vanish.

tests.name: finite
tests.statement: For |I|=2 and |J|=3, both sides are six spheres and the coordinate (1,2) projection is the tensor of those two projections.

tests.name: symmetry
tests.statement: Swapping two degree-one suspended sphere factors multiplies the generator by −1; unsuspended coordinate reindexing has sign +1.

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.splitFiniteFreeSphereTower
targets.statement: A split finite free sphere tower is a functor P:ℕᵒᵖ→Sp with a finite sphere basis at each stage, a sphere-linear section s_n:P_n→P_(n+1) of each transition d_n, and coherent choices identifying composites with their iterated splittings. Maps are coherent maps of diagrams; a map need not preserve the chosen sections. Construct the coherent identification of P_n with P_0 plus the first n split kernels, each kernel a finite free sphere module, and hence lim δP as the countable product of these sphere factors.
hypotheses: finite free means a finite coproduct of the unsuspended sphere, not an arbitrary perfect spectrum
the sections are sphere-linear; no coefficient-linearity is inferred

locator.where: Proof of Lemma B.8, printed p.79, Q lines 3672–3674 (split-tower argument)

api.name: splitFiniteFreeSphereTower_mk
api.statement: Finite sphere bases, transitions, sections and coherent right-inverse identities determine a split tower.

api.name: splitFiniteFreeSphereTower_ext
api.statement: Coherently equal stage maps give equal maps of tower limits.

api.name: splitFiniteFreeSphereTower_decompose
api.statement: P_n≃P_0⊕⊕_(r<n)ker d_r and lim δP≃δP_0×∏_rδker d_r.

api.name: splitFiniteFreeSphereTower_changeSplitting
api.statement: Different specified sections give equivalent product presentations of the same limit, compatible with its stage projections.

tests.name: constant
tests.statement: The constant zero tower has every kernel and limit 0; a constant rank-one identity tower has limit 𝕊.

tests.name: growing
tests.statement: For P_n=𝕊^(n+1), the ranks at n=0,1,2 are 1,2,3 and the kernels all have rank 1.

tests.name: non_split
tests.statement: Multiplication by 2 on 𝕊 is not a split surjection: an integer b with 2b=1 does not exist.

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.splitTowerTensorComparison
targets.statement: For any two split finite free sphere towers P,Q, the map (lim_m δP_m)⊗■(lim_n δQ_n)→lim_(m,n)δ(P_m⊗Q_n) induced by stage projections is an equivalence. Restricting the right side to the diagonal n=m is also an equivalence. Both comparisons are natural for all coherent maps of towers, including maps which change the chosen sections.
hypotheses: P,Q carry the data of §3.2

locator.where: Proof of Lemma B.8, printed p.79, Q line 3672

tests.name: constant
tests.statement: Two constant rank-one towers give 𝕊⊗■𝕊≃𝕊.

tests.name: ranks
tests.statement: At m=1,n=2 for the growing rank n+1 towers the independent stage has 2·3=6 summands.

tests.name: scalar_warning
tests.statement: A section of A→A/(t) given by constant polynomials over the sphere is not A-linear: s(t·1)=0 while t·s(1)=t.

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.balancedTensorComparison
targets.statement: For commutative A in Sp■ and A-modules X,Y, construct the natural equivalence X⊗■_A Y≃(X⊗■Y)⊗■_(A⊗■A)A, with the latter action given by multiplication A⊗■A→A. Compute both sides by the supplied two-sided bar constructions and identify their bisimplicial realizations. For maps A→B→C, give coherent identity, associativity and ordinary pushout base-change comparisons of relative tensor. If B is dualizable as an A-module, prove B⊗■_A lim_K M≃lim_K(B⊗■_A M) for every small diagram M. Without this hypothesis, apply balancing to the completed object produced by §3.3; do not move B through its inverse limit.
hypotheses: A,B,C are commutative solid spectral algebras for monoidal module statements
X,Y are A-modules
the inverse-limit assertion assumes B dualizable over A

locator.where: Proof of Lemma B.8, printed pp.79–80, Q lines 3672 and 3685 (spectral application of relative tensor)

tests.name: unit
tests.statement: For A=𝕊 both sides are X⊗■Y; if X=0 both are 0.

tests.name: variables
tests.statement: For A=𝕊[t], X=Y=A, the absolute tensor has π₀=ℤ[t₁,t₂], and balancing sends t₁ and t₂ to t.

tests.name: limit_failure
tests.statement: Over Hℤ, rational scalar extension of ∏_ℕℤ has uniformly bounded denominators. The element (1/2^n)_n lies in ∏_ℕℚ but not in (∏_ℕℤ)⊗ℚ, so arbitrary scalar extension cannot commute with this product.

layers.title: Countable limits and independent support bounds

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.countableLimitOmegaOneFiltered
targets.statement: Let K be a small category whose nerve has countably many nondegenerate simplices, let J be a small ω₁-filtered category, and let F:J×K→Cond(Sp) be any coherent diagram. The comparison colim_j lim_k F(j,k)→lim_k colim_j F(j,k) is an equivalence. Prove the same assertion in Sp■ and in left modules over any fixed E₁ solid spectral algebra. In these categories ω₁-filtered colimits of hypersheaves are computed sectionwise.
hypotheses: K has a countable nerve in the specified sense; J is ω₁-filtered, including nonemptiness
the algebra in the module statement is fixed, with no connective hypothesis

locator.where: Proposition 5.3.3.3, printed p.394, HTT line 18705; RC Remark 4.0.3, p.28, RC line 1411; Q line 3688

tests.name: empty_K
tests.statement: For K empty, both sides are 0; for J a point both sides are lim_K F.

tests.name: ordinary_filtered
tests.statement: For F(n,k)=Hℤ when k<n and 0 otherwise, with J=ℕ and discrete K=ℕ, the two π₀ groups are ⊕_ℕℤ and ∏_ℕℤ, respectively.

tests.name: constant
tests.statement: For K a point the map is the identity on colim_J F; no countable product assertion is used in this case.

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.countableIndependentUnions
targets.statement: For a countable family of light solid abelian groups B_j and directed systems of subobjects B_(j,α)⊆B_j, the natural map colim_(α_j)∏_j B_(j,α_j)→∏_j colim_α B_(j,α) is an isomorphism of light solid sheaves. In a countable split tower of finite sphere sums, prove that π_k of its limit is the inverse limit of the π_k sheaves for every integer k, and that every projection is surjective on π_k. These statements provide independent coordinate bounds and eliminate the lim¹ error used in §5.
hypotheses: each subobject index is nonempty and directed
the product and the family of independent choices are countable
the spectral tower has the coherent splittings of §3.2

locator.where: Theorem 2.3.3(1)–(2), pp.12–13, RC line 539; Bosco Lemma A.4 proof, p.93, Bosco lines 3504–3521

tests.name: bounded_denominators
tests.statement: For B_j=ℚ and subgroups (1/n!)ℤ, independent choices include (1/(j+1)!)_j, while the diagonal union has only uniformly bounded denominators.

tests.name: zero
tests.statement: With every B_j=0 both sides are 0; an empty product is also 0 in abelian groups.

tests.name: split_limit
tests.statement: For truncation towers ℤ^(n+1), the projection of ℤ^ℕ to the first n+1 coordinates is onto and lim¹=0.

layers.title: Complete filtered coefficients and spectral null families

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.completeSplitCoefficientDatum
targets.statement: A complete split coefficient datum consists of a connective commutative solid spectral algebra A, elements a_r∈π₀A(*) with a₀=1, representatives and coherent divisibility maps a_s=a_r b_(r,s) for r≤s, and the induced coherent quotient tower B_r=cofib(a_r:A→A). Its unit A→lim_r B_r must be an equivalence. Each B_r, as a condensed spectrum, has a specified equivalence with δP_r for a finite free sphere module, and the transitions are equipped with coherent sphere-linear sections. Define J_r=fib(A→B_r), with its marked map to A, and Λ_a(M)=lim_r cofib(a_r:M→M)=lim_r(M⊗■_A B_r). Quotients here are A-modules; no commutative algebra structure on a cofiber is assumed.
hypotheses: coherence includes b_(r,r)=1 and b_(r,s)b_(s,t)=b_(r,t) together with the corresponding homotopies
a₀=1 gives B₀=0 and J₀=A
finite free sphere stages and their splittings are underlying sphere data, not A-linear data

locator.where: Proof of Lemma B.8, pp.79–80, Q lines 3672–3688 (model for the general spectral datum)

api.name: completeSplitCoefficientDatum_mk
api.statement: The displayed algebra, multiplication representatives, divisibility homotopies, split stages and completeness equivalence determine the datum; equivalent coherent data induce equivalent completions.

api.name: coefficientIdeal_map
api.statement: J_r≃A and its map to A is multiplication by a_r; for r≤s the map J_s→J_r is multiplication by b_(r,s).

api.name: derivedQuotientCompletion_unit
api.statement: There is a natural map M→Λ_a(M), and scalar-linear maps commute with it and with all quotient projections.

api.name: derivedQuotientCompletion_cofinal
api.statement: A cofinal reindexing of the coherent tower induces an equivalence of completions, compatible with the unit.

api.name: derivedQuotientCompletion_tensor
api.statement: The quotient cofiber of multiplication on M is M⊗■_A B_r; the statement concerns modules and uses no quotient algebra.

tests.name: formal_variable
tests.statement: Construct A as lim_r δ(𝕊[t]/t^r), whose underlying split stages have ranks r and preserve all sphere stems. Multiplication by t has cofiber 𝕊.

tests.name: zero_ring
tests.statement: A=0 with its unique unit and zero stages is admitted; all J_r and all completions are 0.

tests.name: p_moore
tests.statement: The tower 𝕊/p^r is not a split finite free sphere tower: π₀(𝕊/p)=ℤ/p is not finite free over ℤ. The p-adic theorem is §6.4, with its separate hypotheses.

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.properProfile
targets.statement: A proper profile is a function f:ℕ→ℕ such that for every r the set {j | f(j)<r} is finite. Order profiles by an arrow f→g when f(j)≥g(j) for every j. For countable sets I_j define V_f=∏_j∏_(i∈I_j)J_(f(j)), with transition V_f→V_g induced by the marked ideal maps. Define a block map as an A-linear map on the uncompleted direct sums for which each entire input block factors through a specified finite sum of output blocks; include the actual coherent factorizations as data.
hypotheses: j ranges over ℕ; each I_j is countable and may be empty
arrows use reverse pointwise order; properness uses strict f(j)<r

locator.where: Proof of Lemma B.8, p.80, Q lines 3693–3705; Bosco Lemma A.4, p.93, Bosco line 3488

api.name: properProfile_mk
api.statement: A function with the displayed finite-sublevel-set condition determines a profile; equality is pointwise equality.

api.name: properProfile_filtered
api.statement: The profile category is nonempty and filtered, with a common target min(f,g); it is not ω₁-filtered.

api.name: properProfile_transition
api.statement: Identity transitions are identities and transitions compose according to the divisibility coherences.

api.name: finiteSupportBlockMap_comp
api.statement: Identity block maps and composites have finite output supports for each input block.

tests.name: proper
tests.statement: f(j)=j is proper; f(j)=0 fails for r=1, whose sublevel set is all ℕ.

tests.name: empty_blocks
tests.statement: When every I_j is empty, each V_f=0.

tests.name: not_omega_one
tests.statement: The countable family max(j−k,0) has no common target profile, excluding use of §4.1 for this colimit.

tests.name: block_identity_zero
tests.statement: The identity block map has output support {j} on block j; the zero block map has empty support and induces the zero map on every quotient.

tests.name: block_composition
tests.statement: The duplication j↦{2j,2j+1} followed by the same duplication has outputs {4j,4j+1,4j+2,4j+3}, a finite set of size4.

tests.name: profile_transition
tests.statement: For a_r=t^r and f(j)=j+1→g(j)=j, the j-th ideal map sends t^(j+1)x to the same element of t^jA; reversing the inclusion would fail on t^j.

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.spectralNullFamilyComparison
targets.statement: For every complete split coefficient datum and countable block sets I_j, put F_I=⊕_j∏_(i∈I_j)A. Construct a natural equivalence colim_(f proper) V_f→Λ_a(F_I) in Sp■, hence also in Cond(Sp) and on underlying spectra at the point. Its map modulo a_r is obtained by retaining the finitely many blocks with f(j)<r; blocks with f(j)≥r map to zero by the specified divisibility nullhomotopies. The equivalence is of spectra, not just a π₀ identification.
hypotheses: all the hypotheses of §5.1, without any arithmetic specialization
all I_j are countable; the block index is ℕ

locator.where: Proof of Lemma B.8, p.80, Q line 3688 and displayed formula Q lines 3693–3705; Bosco Lemma A.4 proof, Bosco lines 3504–3521 (abelian model)

tests.name: t_decay
tests.statement: For I_j a singleton and A=𝕊[[t]], the family (t^j)_j occurs, whereas (1)_j does not; modulo t^r only j<r remain.

tests.name: finite_blocks
tests.statement: If only blocks 0 and 1 are nonempty singletons, both sides are A²: choose a proper profile with f(0)=f(1)=0.

tests.name: infinite_block
tests.statement: For I₀=ℕ and all other blocks empty, both sides are ∏_ℕA. The allowed zero value at j=0 does not force decay within that block.

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.nullFamilyHomotopyNaturality
targets.statement: For every integer k, the equivalence of §5.3 induces π_kΛ_a(F_I)≃colim_f∏_j∏_(i∈I_j)π_kJ_(f(j)) as light solid homotopy sheaves. It is natural for the coherent finite-output block maps of §5.2 and for maps of complete split coefficient data which carry their marked ideal towers to each other. Under a block map, sums over input blocks are defined by their finite reductions modulo each a_r, not by an unqualified infinite sum in A.
hypotheses: k∈ℤ, with no exclusion of positive or negative degrees
coefficient changes include the coherent quotient maps and their compatibility with the completeness equivalences

locator.where: Proof of Lemma B.8, p.80, Q lines 3688–3705; Bosco Lemma A.4 proof, p.93, Bosco line 3510 (models for spectral extension)

tests.name: negative
tests.statement: For k<0 every term is 0 because the split coefficient ideals are connective; the completed free block sum is connective.

tests.name: sphere_stem
tests.statement: For A=𝕊[[t]], π₁A=(ℤ/2)[[t]] and the degree-one family (ηt^j) has modulo t² survivors η and ηt.

tests.name: block_maps
tests.statement: The map sending input block j to blocks 2j and 2j+1 sends t^j to two copies of t^j; modulo t² only outputs 0,1,2,3 survive. A block mapped simultaneously to every output is excluded by the finite-output condition.

layers.title: Bounded-below resolutions, realizations and prime completion

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.boundedBelowFreeResolution
targets.statement: For a connective E₁ solid algebra A and M∈Mod_A with π_kM=0 for k<b, construct an augmented simplicial resolution P•→M whose realization is M and each P_n is a coproduct of shifts Σ^dG_A with d≥b. The same integer b works for every simplicial degree. Give coherent comparison maps between resolutions over a map of modules, unique at the level of their realized derived functors; no uniqueness of the individual free presentations is asserted. Arbitrary coproduct index sets remain in the fixed universe.
hypotheses: A connective; b∈ℤ; M≥b
E₁ suffices; no commutativity or arithmetic completeness is required

locator.where: Proof of Proposition A.3, pp.92–93, Bosco lines 3462–3469; Q proof of Lemma B.8, Q lines 3688–3692 (integer/arithmetic resolution models)

tests.name: zero
tests.statement: M=0 has the zero resolution and realization0.

tests.name: shift
tests.statement: For M=Σ^bG_A the constant simplicial object on M is already a resolution with lower bound b.

tests.name: no_uniform_bound
tests.statement: The family Σ^(−n)G_A has no common lower bound; it does not satisfy the hypothesis of the realization theorem for completion.

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.quotientCompletionConnectivity
targets.statement: For any connective commutative solid A and coherent divisibility tower of scalar multiplication maps a_r, define Λ_a by the module cofiber tower as in §5.1, without assuming finite free quotients or that A is complete. It is exact, and if M≥b then M/a_r≥b for every r and Λ_a(M)≥b−1. For the free block modules of §5.3 and a complete split datum, improve the bound to Λ_a(F_I)≥0 by split surjectivity on each homotopy tower. The map between the limit and the product has the fiber-of-1−shift convention of the supplied tower theory.
hypotheses: A connective, b∈ℤ; all maps of the scalar tower include coherent homotopies
only the improved bound requires the split datum

locator.where: Proposition A.3 proof, Bosco line 3465; Q proof of Lemma B.8, Q line 3688 (connectivity step made explicit)

tests.name: unit_scalar
tests.statement: For a_r=1 all quotient cofibers and Λ_aM are0.

tests.name: zero_scalar
tests.statement: For a single zero scalar the derived quotient is M⊕ΣM; it is not the ordinary quotient M alone.

tests.name: lim_error
tests.statement: For the tower ℤ --2→ ℤ --2→⋯ in degree0, lim=0 and lim¹=ℤ₂/ℤ, so the homotopy limit has π₋₁=ℤ₂/ℤ. The b−1 bound is necessary for general towers.

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.quotientCompletionRealization
targets.statement: For the quotient completion functor of §6.2 and a simplicial A-module M• with M_n≥b for one integer b independent of n, the natural map |Λ_a(M•)|→Λ_a(|M•|) is an equivalence. More explicitly, cofib(|sk_dM•|→|M•|) lies in degrees ≥b+d+1, and applying Λ_a gives degrees ≥b+d; the analogous tail of |Λ_a(M•)| is ≥b+d. Consequently finite skeleta determine the comparison on π_k once d>k−b+2. The equivalence is natural and agrees with the balanced bar comparison of §3.4 whenever A and the bar terms have the stated uniform lower bounds. For a two-sided bar for X⊗_A Y, take the A-action through the X factor in each degree; the realized action is the balanced A-action, and the comparison is A-linear for these specified actions.
hypotheses: A connective and M_n≥b for all n
the quotient tower is fixed across all simplicial degrees
for a two-sided bar, coefficient algebra is connective and its two modules have fixed lower bounds
d is a natural skeleton degree, and bounds involving b,k,d are inequalities in ℤ

locator.where: Proof of Proposition A.3, Bosco line 3465; Q proof of Lemma B.8, Q lines 3688–3692 (uniform spectral estimate supplied here)

tests.name: constant
tests.statement: A constant simplicial M gives the identity comparison Λ_aM→Λ_aM.

tests.name: first_layer
tests.statement: A normalized layer in simplicial degree1 contributes ΣM, so a b-connective input produces a (b+1)-connective layer before completion and at least b-connective after completion.

tests.name: uniform
tests.statement: With normalized term Σ^(−n)A in degree n, its suspended layer is A in every degree; the tails never become more connective, so the proof cannot apply.

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.boundedBelowPrimeCompleteComparison
targets.statement: For every prime p, define e_p(X)=lim_r δ(X/p^r) on derived p-complete ordinary spectra X. Evaluation at the point is its right adjoint on p-complete objects and the unit is an equivalence, so e_p is fully faithful. If M,N are p-complete bounded-below solid spectra then M⊗■N is p-complete. For bounded-below p-complete X,Y, e_p(X)⊗■e_p(Y)≃e_p((X⊗Y)^∧_p). The bounded-below p-complete solid category is symmetric monoidal with unit e_p(𝕊^∧_p), and the inclusion into all solid spectra is lax monoidal with unit map δ𝕊→e_p(𝕊^∧_p). On Hℤ-linear inputs, recover Bosco’s completed-tensor comparison over any derived p-complete solid ordinary ring with bounded-above cohomological complexes. Construct the p-complete full subcategory in Cond(Sp) and Sp■ by orthogonality to all shifts of p-inverted free spectral objects, and prove its reflection is the p-power cofiber limit used in the definition of e_p.
hypotheses: p is any prime, including 2 and 3
full faithfulness has no lower-bound restriction; the tensor statements do
the ordinary and solid p-completions use derived cofibers

locator.where: Paragraph 2.2, p.11, W lines 452–462; Bosco Proposition A.3, pp.92–93, Bosco line 3459

api.name: primeCompleteDiscrete_unit
api.statement: For a p-complete spectrum X, evaluation e_pX at * is X, compatibly with the completed discrete/evaluation adjunction unit.

api.name: primeCompleteDiscrete_tensor
api.statement: For bounded-below complete X,Y the tensor comparison is computed with completed ordinary smash and has completed sphere unit.

api.name: primeCompleteInteger_comparison
api.statement: On the Hℤ-linear realization the comparison is Bosco’s relative completed tensor over the chosen derived p-complete solid ordinary ring.

api.name: solidPrimeCompletion_reflection
api.statement: The p-power cofiber limit is left adjoint to inclusion of objects right-orthogonal to every shift of every p-inverted light free object.

tests.name: p2
tests.statement: At p=2, π₀(e_p(𝕊^∧_p)(*))=ℤ₂, and the ambient unit has π₀=ℤ.

tests.name: p3
tests.statement: At p=3 the same calculation gives ℤ₃, and the unit comparison sends 1 to1; no inversion of 2 or 3 is used.

tests.name: integer_model
tests.statement: For M=N=Hℤ_p the relative solid tensor over Hℤ is Hℤ_p. In contrast H𝔽_p⊗_{Hℤ_p}H𝔽_p has an additional π₁=𝔽_p; absolute sphere tensor and Hℤ-relative tensor remain distinct.

tests.name: characteristic_p
tests.statement: For X=H𝔽_p, X/p^r=X⊕ΣX with transition identity on X and zero on ΣX. The limit is X and the completion unit is its identity, including p=2,3.

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.spectralAnalyticStructure
targets.statement: For connective commutative A in Sp■ define an uncompleted spectral analytic structure to be a specified accessible reflective stable full subcategory D⊆Mod_A(Sp■), closed under all small ambient limits and colimits and under internal Hom_A(C,M) for arbitrary A-module C and M∈D, whose reflector L_D preserves connective objects. A completed structure additionally has A∈D. A morphism (A,D)→(B,E) is an algebra map A→B whose restriction carries E into D. Equivalent reflective full subcategories determine the same structure only with their actual inclusion and unit identified.
hypotheses: A is connective and commutative; size bounds are fixed
reflectivity and accessibility are explicit data/properties; no reflection principle is assumed without proof

locator.where: Definition 4.1.1 and Remark 4.1.2, pp.28–29, RC lines 1431 and 1457; AG Definition 12.1, AG line 3014 (integer/animated model)

api.name: spectralAnalyticStructure_mk
api.statement: The specified inclusion, accessible adjunction, closure laws and connective-preservation proof determine the structure.

api.name: spectralAnalyticStructure_ext
api.statement: Two inclusions with the same full image have a uniquely identified reflector under their units; an unmarked equivalence of abstract categories is insufficient.

api.name: spectralAnalyticStructure_morphism
api.statement: Identity and composite algebra maps preserving complete objects give identity and composite morphisms.

api.name: spectralAnalyticStructure_complete
api.statement: The structure is completed iff its unit A→L_DA is an equivalence.

tests.name: trivial
tests.statement: For D=all modules, L_D=id and the structure is completed.

tests.name: zero
tests.statement: D={0} is an uncompleted structure for every A, completed exactly when A=0.

tests.name: hom_closure
tests.statement: The full subcategory of perfect Hℤ-modules fails the axioms: a countable coproduct of Hℤ is not perfect.

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.analyticCompletedTensor
targets.statement: For an uncompleted structure (A,D), construct the closed symmetric monoidal tensor M⊗hat_A N=L_D(M⊗■_A N) on D, with unit L_DA and internal Hom inherited from Mod_A. Retain the connective commutative coefficient algebra Â=L_DA supplied by the lax monoidal inclusion and its map A→Â; no identification with A is made without completedness. For a morphism (A,D)→(B,E), completed scalar extension M↦L_E(B⊗■_A M) is left adjoint to restriction E→D. Prove identity, composition and coherences for the scalar-change squares: both iterated extensions along a coherently commuting square to a fixed analytic target agree with extension along its composite. For algebra-pushout base change, prove the completed-tensor comparison after applying the target reflector whenever its kernel is the localizing tensor ideal generated by the scalar extensions of the two input kernels; this kernel-generation condition specifies the induced analytic structure. Explicitly, for an algebra pushout B′=B⊗■_A A′ with compatible analytic structures D_B,D_A′,D_B′ and the indicated generated kernel, both L_D_B′(B′⊗_B L_D_B(B⊗_A M)) and L_D_B′(B′⊗_A′ L_D_A′(A′⊗_A M)) are canonically L_D_B′(B′⊗_A M), for every A-module M. These are equivalences of complete B′-modules.
hypotheses: the hypotheses are exactly those of §7.1
base-change squares include their algebra maps and coherence; the pushout assertion has the stated kernel-generation hypothesis

locator.where: Proposition 4.1.6 and proof, pp.29–30, RC lines 1489–1519; AG Proposition 12.4 and Remark 12.5, p.80, AG lines 3041–3055

api.name: analyticCompletedTensor_unit
api.statement: The tensor unit is L_DA, and for completed structures this is A.

api.name: analyticScalarExtension_adjunction
api.statement: For M∈D and N∈E, Map_E(L_E(B⊗_A M),N)≃Map_D(M,U N).

api.name: analyticScalarExtension_comp
api.statement: For composable compatible maps, L_F(C⊗_B L_E(B⊗_A M))≃L_F(C⊗_A M), coherently under units and threefold composition.

api.name: analyticScalarExtension_baseChange
api.statement: For the compatible algebra pushout B′=B⊗_A A′, the two completed scalar paths displayed in the statement agree with L_D_B′(B′⊗_A M) for every A-module M, coherently with the units.

tests.name: zero_module
tests.statement: 0⊗hat_A N=0 and every completed scalar extension sends0 to0.

tests.name: uncompleted_unit
tests.statement: For D=0 and A=Hℤ, the tensor unit has π₀=0 rather than ℤ.

tests.name: derived_base_change
tests.statement: For trivial structures the base-change comparison is the derived relative tensor, retaining Tor in the square ℤ→𝔽₂←ℤ.

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.spectralSummabilityLocalization
targets.statement: For connective commutative solid A and any small family F⊆π₀A(*), construct the full subcategory D_F of modules M for which 1−fσ* is invertible on internal Hom_A(A⊗■G,M), for every f∈F. Prove D_F is an uncompleted spectral analytic structure, including ambient colimit closure and connective preservation of its reflector. The condition can equivalently be tested with A⊗N in condensed modules. Construct its free complete modules, its reflector, and its coefficient algebra Â_F=L_FA with the unit A→Â_F. Establish naturality for algebra maps which carry the specified summability tests to tests of the target. Imposing more tests gives a further localization; being completed is a separate assertion that A is itself F-summable.
hypotheses: F is small; f acts through its specified π₀ scalar action
all internal Hom tests are internal equivalences, rather than only equations on global π₀

locator.where: Paragraph 4.2, p.41, MW lines 1764–1775; RC Example 4.6.4(2),(4), p.44, RC lines 2125–2145 (integer model)

api.name: spectralSummabilityLocalization_tests
api.statement: M is local exactly when all specified internal 1−fσ* maps are equivalences; equivalent scalar representatives give equivalent tests.

api.name: spectralSummabilityLocalization_free
api.statement: The free complete object on an A-module C is L_FC, with Map(L_FC,M)≃Map(C,M) for local M.

api.name: spectralSummabilityLocalization_monotone
api.statement: For F⊆F′, D_F′⊆D_F and L_F′L_F≃L_F′, with the units fixed.

api.name: spectralSummabilityLocalization_scalar
api.statement: A map carrying the scalar tests into a target family makes restriction preserve local objects and gives the completed extension of §7.2.

api.name: spectralSummability_nilpotent
api.statement: If f^d=0 for some d≥1, the f-test is automatically invertible on every module, with inverse the finite geometric sum of the powers of fσ*.

tests.name: zero_scalar
tests.statement: F=∅ and F={0} both give all modules; f=1 adds no condition in Sp■.

tests.name: two_term_sign
tests.statement: For a finite-support null sequence b=e₁ and any discrete scalar f, (1−fσ*)(e₁+fe₀)=e₁.

tests.name: coefficient_changes
tests.statement: For A=Hℚ_p with its topological solid realization and f=1/p, the null sequence b_n=p^n satisfies b_n−f b_(n+1)=0 and b₀=1. Thus A is not F-complete, including p=2,3, and replacing Â_F by A would be false.

tests.name: nilpotent
tests.statement: For A=H(𝔽₂[ε]/ε²) and f=ε, the inverse is 1+εσ* and the reflector is the identity; this tests a nonreduced characteristic-two coefficient ring.

targets.name: SolidAnalyticRings.analyticMeasureSpectralComparison
targets.statement: For an integer-linear analytic measure structure (B,μ) supplied by VS2.2, with B and all measure objects in its integer-solid realization, and represented on its common size-bounded light presentation, transport its complete derived module subcategory through §2.3 to the Hℤ-linear spectral algebra associated to B. Prove this is a completed spectral analytic structure exactly when the imported Dirac unit B→μ[*] is an equivalence; in general retain μ[*] as the completed coefficient algebra. Identify free complete modules, Dirac maps, relative tensor, internal Hom and compatible scalar extension. For animated B use θB and the supplied animated-module comparison, retaining the distinction from arbitrary Hℤ-algebras. Prove these comparisons commute with cutoff enlargement on the supplied common presentations and with restriction to the light site on those presentations; no equivalence of unrestricted condensed universes is asserted.
hypotheses: the measure structure and its enhanced derived realization are supplied by VS2.2
site comparison is confined to the size-bounded presentations on which that supplier proves free-object and tensor/Hom comparison
animated B is carried by θ, rather than identified with arbitrary CAlg(Mod_Hℤ)
B and μ[S] have the imported integer-solid realization; this comparison concerns the solid measure structures of VS2.2

locator.where: Definition 6.12 and Proposition 6.14, pp.39–40, AG lines 1361 and 1384; Definition 12.1, Proposition 12.4, Remark 12.5, pp.79–80, AG lines 3014–3055

tests.name: finite_measures
tests.statement: For integer-solid measures on a finite set of size2 the free complete module is ℤ²; on ∅ it is0 and on * it isℤ.

tests.name: denominators
tests.statement: For topological E/ℚ_p, (∏_I O_E)[1/p] has uniformly bounded denominators and excludes (p^(−n))_n. Replacing the free complete measure object by an unrestricted product ∏_I E fails.

tests.name: positive_characteristic
tests.statement: Over 𝔽₂, θ preserves the specified animated polynomial input but is not an equivalence onto all commutative H𝔽₂-algebras; the positive group homology witness is retained.

suppliers.what: Concrete symmetric spectra, stable and monoidal models, sphere and Eilenberg–Mac Lane adapters; coherent ordinary spectral towers and derived prime completion.
Operadic and module model comparisons, cochain homology/spectrum homotopy with π_k=H^(−k), cellular approximation and connective-model comparison; no new spectrum carrier.

Stable enhancements, hypercovers, accessibility, localization, coherent towers, bar scalar extension, monoidal localization, monadicity and spectrum/module comparisons. The additional cardinal-interchange contract is gap:cardinal-interchange.
Integer solidification and enhanced derived solid tensor; analytic measures, complete modules and proved size-bounded site comparisons. The additional light AB6 contract is gap:light-countable-ab6.

consumers.what: §§2.8–2.12 consume §§1–6 for the light-solid-spectra gap, split tower and balanced tensor inputs, completed block sums, all homotopy sheaves and bounded-below realizations. Its arithmetic idempotence and multiplicative profile estimates remain there.
§§6.2–6.4 import §§1–2 and §6.4 for the relocated light spectral foundations and bounded-below p-complete comparison; trace classes, nuclearity, even sites and filtrations remain there.

Contracts R23–R24 can use §7.2 scalar change and §7.4 common-presentation comparison. Huber-pair localization, formal complements and nonarchimedean geometric claims require their existing VS2.2 ownership or a Part II extension.

LR.3 can use §7.4 for the supplied integer-linear E-coefficient comparison. Profinite group rings, strongly inaccessible-cutoff equivalences and Banach/Smith comparison are not outputs of this light spectral roadmap.

gaps.title: Abstract cardinal-filtered colimits and cardinal-small limits
gaps.detail: EnhancedDerivedSheaves E0.8 defines cardinal filteredness and presentability, while E5:presentability.2 constructs spectra; the read sections do not state the general HTT Proposition 5.3.3.3 equivalence. Import its formal proof as an extension in that roadmap’s direction, then specialize it here to countable hypercover descent. The source is read: HTT line 18705.
gaps.needs: For every infinite regular κ and κ-filtered small J, colim_J in spaces preserves every κ-small limit, with a compatible levelwise stabilization comparison.
gaps.section: E0.8 and E5:presentability.2; proposed EnhancedDerivedSheaves, Part II, cardinal interchange

gaps.title: Countable independent directed unions in the light abelian carrier
gaps.detail: The pinned Light/AB.lean gives countable exact products and Grothendieck abelianness, not countable AB6. VS2.1 supplies abelian solidity and its enhancement, but the read contract does not state RC Theorem 2.3.3(1)’s independent-union law. Its extension belongs to the integer/light abelian owner. This is the precise abelian input to the spectral null-family proof, not an appeal to ω₁-filteredness of profiles.
gaps.needs: For countably many directed systems of subobjects in light condensed abelian groups, independent choices commute with their product, naturally and compatibly with the solid full inclusion.
gaps.section: VS2.1; proposed VStackSheavesAndLisseCategoriesPartIII §1.1, light countable AB6
